title: single material with cpc as a parseable numeric string and hosted https creative assets

source.name: Kadam Feed and RTB contracts, including in-page and clickunder examples
source.notes: All source records are retained in assets/sources.json by reference.sourceIds.

modifications: All ids, domains, prices, timestamps, creative text and URLs independently authored.

cpc is deliberately a numeric string ("0.0175") rather than a JSON number — many SSPs send it this way and Core's own field contract (rules-feed.js) explicitly tolerates and flags it, distinct from a non-numeric string.

icon_url/image_url are hosted https URLs (not data: URIs), so the preview's initial sealed state stays blocked-with-limitation — the deliberate counterpart to push-x-kadam-material-single's full-render data: URI case.
No OpenRTB or GET-URL request is invented for this response-only scenario: no registered decoder recognizes a Kadam-style feed request query string (push-kadam-icon-notice, known gap DEF-107).
provenance.sanitized: No real visitor or subscriber data. All URLs use reserved .test hostnames; icon_url/image_url are placeholder addresses that the preview's content policy never fetches automatically.

pairApplicability.note: Response-only: no registered decoder recognizes the Kadam feed's GET request shape (DEF-107), so only the documented single-object response material shape is exercised here.

response.title: Fresh paint for the porch
response.text: A weekend project told in one card.

specNotes: rules-feed.js's 3-tier cpc/price contract (formats-feeds map §1.1/§2) distinguishes missing, wrong-type-but-parseable, and wrong-type-unparseable: a numeric string such as "0.0175" is parseable and must warn, not error — this is documented Core behavior being asserted as correct, not a gap.

Desired capability: detectFeedFormat recognizes a cleanly-validated, documented push material as push regardless of whether its image/icon keys carry the `_url` suffix. Existing product acceptance is not the validity oracle.

Remote https creative assets stay blocked in the initial sealed preview; the title and description text remain visible inline on the synthetic card regardless (spec 014 FR-001/FR-005) — this is the documented "partial" render, not a missing-creative failure.
The documented vendor ad type must be identified in the merged format result. Public Core vocabulary uses pops for pop traffic; this is a vendor capability expectation, not an invented IAB extension.
notes: Core observations in the source archive were deliberately excluded from expectations. Protocol metadata may describe a vendor-specific 2.x carrier; it does not claim a normative minor-version inference.

preview.limitation: Remote creative assets are blocked by the preview content policy.
preview.capabilityGap: Images remain blocked in the initial sealed preview; request interception does not bypass CSP.
